newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse says client default rumour untrue.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse says client default rumour untrue.

text.p: The Thai stock exchange on Thursday denied market rumours that some brokerages were hit by client defaults on margin loans, which forced a sharp drop in shares during the bourse's afternoon session.

"There is a rumour that some members of the exchange have financial problems from margin loans given to their clients. The SET would like to explain that the rumour is untrue according to exchange supervision," the bourse said in a statement.
Despite the exchange's denial of the rumour the SET index was down 3.05 percent or 32.02 points at 1,017.72 at 0928 GMT.
Thai stock prices fell sharply after the lunch break on selling linked to rumours that at least four finance and brokerage firms were hit by client loan defaults.
Two major listed brokerages, Adkinson Securities, International Trust and Finance, fell their 10 percent daily limit during the slide earlier in the afternoon session.
Adkinson Securities fell three baht to 27.25 and International Trust and Finance one baht to 9.50 baht.
Also down the 10 percent limit were Sitca Investment and Securities which fell 2,75 baht to 26.75 and Dynamic Eastern Finance and Securities, which dropped 2 baht to 19.
Some analysts said the Thai stock market's prolonged slump could have triggered such rumours. Sentiment has been poor over past weeks as local political and economic concerns hang over the bourse.

Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa faces a non-confidence motion launched by the opposition on September 18, Moody's on Tuesday downgraded Thailand's short-term sovereign debt ratings and exports growth has been very sluggish in the first seven months of this year.
